purpose: Fexofenadine is used to relieve allergy symptoms like sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes, and hives. It works for both seasonal allergies (like hay fever) and skin reactions. It helps you feel more comfortable when your body is reacting to things like pollen, dust, or pet dander.
how_it_works: When you come into contact with something you are allergic to, your body releases a chemical called histamine, which causes those annoying allergy symptoms. Fexofenadine blocks the receptors that histamine attaches to, so the symptoms are reduced. Unlike older antihistamines, it is designed to stay out of your brain, which is why it usually does not make you feel sleepy.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication very well. The most common side effects are headache, stomach upset, nausea, or feeling tired. Some people may notice back pain or a mild cold-like feeling.
warnings: Avoid drinking fruit juices like grapefruit, orange, or apple juice within 4 hours of taking this medicine because they can reduce how well it works — take it with plain water instead. If you have kidney problems, talk to your doctor or pharmacist before using it. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Avoid taking it with antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium at the same time.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 12 and older, the usual dose is 60 mg twice a day or 180 mg once a day. For children ages 6 to 11, the typical dose is 30 mg twice a day. Always take it with a full glass of water, not juice. Follow the directions on your package or as advised by your doctor or pharmacist.
